name: technical
question: ¿Puede /restore de Linde recuperar una cuenta cerrada?

messages.content: ¿Puede /restore de Linde recuperar una cuenta cerrada?

response.answer:
## Respuesta directa

No. Según la documentación de Linde disponible, el endpoint `/restore` recupera elementos eliminados, pero **no** cuentas cerradas. Así lo afirma de forma consistente el archivo de referencia en todas las versiones lingüísticas consultadas: «El endpoint /restore recupera elementos borrados, pero no cuentas cerradas» ([fixture 25](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0)), y la misma formulación aparece en inglés ([fixture 20](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A675879258dcb3e6a835b42863551a6db292065a442a236cf765cf78e9f4937a8%3A0)), en francés ([fixture 15](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A95afb0f98bc130f1dc8d780686f3b7c7e0f754f158f307ee93cb450e65b657bf%3A0)), en alemán ([fixture 10](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Acc2bc7187edf8af865a07705765f129559817376e3763ae12245b90be2789e68%3A0)), en italiano ([fixture 30](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afc8f8c7272fa2d9ff4f125062dfd320d09c5005a23030d33c84ccd9240b83c23%3A0)) y en portugués ([fixture 05](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Ae661cadd9869d6310ac452888c6113170eb8f2087b0b00abcfdd8aed7b067bde%3A0)). El propio listado estructurado de «Evidence» de uno de los documentos refuerza la misma distinción entre lo que se recupera y lo que no ([fixture 30](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afc8f8c7272fa2d9ff4f125062dfd320d09c5005a23030d33c84ccd9240b83c23%3A0)).

## Matices relevantes

**Alcance de `/restore`.** Se limita a «elementos eliminados» (ítems borrados), no a cuentas cerradas. La distinción es explícita y se repite sin variación en los seis documentos, lo que sugiere que se trata de una limitación de diseño y no de una ambigüedad de redacción.

**Ventana temporal.** La API Linde conserva los eventos durante **14 días**, lo que enmarca el periodo en el que tiene sentido solicitar una restauración ([fixture 25](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0); [fixture 20](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A675879258dcb3e6a835b42863551a6db292065a442a236cf765cf78e9f4937a8%3A0)).

**Cambio de versión.** La versión 2 amplió ese plazo de 7 a 14 días ([fixture 10](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Acc2bc7187edf8af865a07705765f129559817376e3763ae12245b90be2789e68%3A0); [fixture 30](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afc8f8c7272fa2d9ff4f125062dfd320d09c5005a23030d33c84ccd9240b83c23%3A0)), dato que puede importar si se está trabajando con una instancia antigua, aunque no altera la respuesta sobre cuentas cerradas.

## Cómo leer la evidencia

Las seis fuentes citadas no son estudios independientes que converjan: son el mismo texto de archivo reproducido en distintos idiomas, con la etiqueta de procedencia «Nodus QA synthetic archive» visible en varios de ellos ([fixture 25](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0); [fixture 05](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Ae661cadd9869d6310ac452888c6113170eb8f2087b0b00abcfdd8aed7b067bde%3A0)). Por tanto, la coincidencia entre ellas **no multiplica la fuerza probatoria**: es una única afirmación replicada. No hay en el material consultado un documento de especificación oficial de la API Linde ni una descripción del comportamiento de `/restore` ante una cuenta cerrada que contradiga esta nota.

## Sobre el resto del material recuperado

La búsqueda trajo también pasajes ajenos a la pregunta —el sensor Alba y su calibración ([fixture 13](nodus://passage/scoped%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Af8211fcf3299019c17aaba1dba8de8fcb1aedd6ec5c7505a73ed629679156b46); [idea](nodus://idea/g-0001)), los ensayos de recuperación espaciada ([fixture 07](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Ace34be62f4e64bd67814a4cf354a630700db6204d6a75df37f85216dc451c53c%3A0); [fixture 02](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A1d8054029e99a5e3a726df408aad2e82405877f366c3a7686bb8476f0709af3b%3A0); [fixture 12](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A14842f05c2569b8d9b25fef34de5eb41a54477d009ed95553588468a20f61ba2%3A0)), la historia de Puerto Claro ([fixture 01](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A79abbae88ed29e18f22703e915529f640bd6e3dc99f3afc260762c9d310fc6ce%3A0); [fixture 06](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A1bf1741ed427433b63fa91f4c24a2ec064ca7f6cae0f0061f94653d5f7edac4e%3A0)) y artículos técnicos sobre modelos de lenguaje ([RWKV](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A0afe0e1473ace2888063fec061f5b2b1868f11fcf2f28932bd31ed4a6270779e%3A37); [DPO](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A37176225006b63db9086cc3d3dfcdc65d1314cb7b4fd1248830f39c9b3eaa14b%3A0); [LLaMA](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Ae13f58cdb4b0248f6b3d04b01263633785c1b07ba87ca5a4912d0313a96c73ad%3A59)). Ninguno de ellos aborda el comportamiento de `/restore` frente a cuentas cerradas, por lo que no aportan a la pregunta.

## Conclusión

**No**, `/restore` no puede recuperar una cuenta cerrada en Linde: solo restaura elementos eliminados dentro de la ventana de retención de 14 días ([fixture 25](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3Afbccb7ff3612d283e7bae388db6100e71002eb821965768c22fa6eacb02ffc07%3A0); [fixture 20](nodus://passage/documentary%3A78278955b26cc982df2f3d215880592b6234164a69bbff726506daa251653a46%3A675879258dcb3e6a835b42863551a6db292065a442a236cf765cf78e9f4937a8%3A0)). Si necesitas un mecanismo alternativo para cuentas cerradas, el material consultado no lo describe; sería un hueco a verificar contra la documentación oficial de Linde.

# Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model Rafael Rafailov∗† Archit Sharma∗† Eric Mitchell∗† Stefano Ermon†‡ Christopher D. Manning† Chelsea Finn† †Stanford University ‡CZ Biohub {rafailov,architsh,eric.mitchell}@cs.stanford.edu ## Abstract While large-scale unsupervised language models (LMs) learn broad world knowledge and some reasoning skills, achieving precise control of their behavior is difficult due to the completely unsupervised nature of their training. Existing methods for gaining such steerability collect human labels of the relative quality of model generations and fine-tune the unsupervised LM to align with these preferences, often with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, RLHF is a complex and often unstable procedure, first fitting a reward model that reflects the human preferences, and then fine-tuning the large unsupervised LM using reinforcement learning to maximize this estimated reward without drifting too far from the original model. In this paper we introduce a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss. The resulting algorithm, which we call Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), is stable, performant, and computationally lightweight, eliminating the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning. Our experiments show that DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods. Notably, fine-tuning with DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations, and matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train. arXiv:2305.18290v3 [cs.LG] 29 Jul 2024 ## 1 Introduction Large unsupervised language models (LMs) trained on very large

# Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model Rafael Rafailov∗† Archit Sharma∗† Eric Mitchell∗† Stefano Ermon†‡ Christopher D. Manning† Chelsea Finn† †Stanford University ‡CZ Biohub {rafailov,architsh,eric.mitchell}@cs.stanford.edu ## Abstract While large-scale unsupervised language models (LMs) learn broad world knowledge and some reasoning skills, achieving precise control of their behavior is difficult due to the completely unsupervised nature of their training. Existing methods for gaining such steerability collect human labels of the relative quality of model generations and fine-tune the unsupervised LM to align with these preferences, often with reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). However, RLHF is a complex and often unstable procedure, first fitting a reward model that reflects the human preferences, and then fine-tuning the large unsupervised LM using reinforcement learning to maximize this estimated reward without drifting too far from the original model. In this paper we introduce a new parameterization of the reward model in RLHF that enables extraction of the corresponding optimal policy in closed form, allowing us to solve the standard RLHF problem with only a simple classification loss. The resulting algorithm, which we call Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), is stable, performant, and computationally lightweight, eliminating the need for sampling from the LM during fine-tuning or performing significant hyperparameter tuning. Our experiments show that DPO can fine-tune LMs to align with human preferences as well as or better than existing methods. Notably, fine-tuning with DPO exceeds PPO-based RLHF in ability to control sentiment of generations, and matches or improves response quality in summarization and single-turn dialogue while being substantially simpler to implement and train. arXiv:2305.18290v3 [cs.LG] 29 Jul 2024 ## 1 Introduction Large unsupervised language models (LMs) trained on very large
